purpose: Carve second-ring neurobiology that would overload the canonical whole-brain atlas: cranial nerves, hypothalamic nuclei, brainstem nuclei, hippocampal subfields, cerebellar microcircuitry, pain systems, neurovascular coupling, development/aging, language/social cognition and predictive-processing theory.
epistemic_rule: This file deepens biology first. Potatoverse symbolism is added only where it clarifies an existing canonical mapping; theoretical neuroscience is labelled theory rather than anatomy.

clusters.name: Cranial nerves and brain-body interfaces
clusters.summary: Twelve paired cranial nerves link the brain to special senses and head/neck visceral, somatic and autonomic functions. Ten have nuclei associated with the brainstem; olfactory and optic systems are forebrain special-sensory pathways.

nerves.name: Olfactory
nerves.central_relation: olfactory bulb/cortex rather than a brainstem nucleus

nerves.name: Trigeminal
nerves.central_relation: large sensory nuclear complex spanning brainstem plus motor nucleus

nerves.name: Facial
nerves.core: facial expression, taste anterior tongue, lacrimal/salivary control

nerves.name: Glossopharyngeal
nerves.core: pharyngeal sensation, posterior-tongue taste, carotid body/sinus input, parotid control

nerves.name: Vagus
nerves.core: visceral sensation and parasympathetic regulation; laryngeal/pharyngeal motor functions
nerves.central_relation: medullary nuclei including nucleus tractus solitarius, dorsal motor nucleus and nucleus ambiguus

nerves.name: Accessory
nerves.central_relation: spinal accessory nucleus with cranial historical complexities

clusters.functional_columns: Brainstem cranial-nerve nuclei can be understood by sensory/motor and somatic/visceral functional columns rather than by memorizing twelve isolated cables.
clusters.project_relation: Cranial nerves are useful as literal biological doors/interfaces between brain and world/body, but no single cranial nerve is the canonical Potatoverse Door.
clusters.boundary: Do not turn vagal or cranial-nerve anatomy into a one-to-one chakra or Spirit map.

clusters.name: Hypothalamic nuclei and homeostatic control
clusters.summary: The hypothalamus is not one thermostat. Distinct nuclei and neuronal populations coordinate circadian timing, endocrine outputs, temperature, feeding, fluid balance, reproduction, autonomic state and defensive/social behaviors.

systems.name: Suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN)
systems.relation: SCN → multisynaptic autonomic pathway → pineal melatonin timing

clusters.project_relation: This deeper anatomy strengthens the Steward metaphor: the hypothalamus is a distributed household-management system rather than the Father's House itself.
clusters.boundary: Nucleus names and functions overlap; project roles must not be assigned one-to-one to every hypothalamic nucleus.

clusters.name: Brainstem nuclei, autonomic columns and neuromodulatory hubs
clusters.summary: Brainstem gray matter is organized as nuclei embedded among ascending/descending tracts. Many life-support, sensory, motor and state systems are concentrated here.
clusters.project_relation: The Lower Gate becomes more biologically precise when separated into autonomic life-support, orienting, pain/defense and arousal/neuromodulatory subsystems.
clusters.boundary: The brainstem is not a primitive soul layer; its systems participate in sophisticated state, learning and cognition loops.

clusters.name: Hippocampal formation and subfield circuitry
clusters.summary: The hippocampal formation contains distinct subfields with recurrent and feedforward motifs important to episodic/contextual memory and spatial representation.

subfields.name: Dentate gyrus
subfields.major_relation: entorhinal input → dentate granule cells → CA3 mossy fibers

subfields.name: CA3
subfields.major_relation: dentate input + recurrent collateral network → CA1 via Schaffer collaterals

subfields.name: CA2
subfields.boundary: Do not reduce CA2 to one social-memory module.

subfields.name: CA1
roles: comparison/integration of hippocampal and entorhinal inputs

subfields.name: Subiculum
roles: hippocampal output/interface with cortical and subcortical targets

subfields.name: Entorhinal cortex
roles: major cortical gateway to/from hippocampal formation

clusters.canonical_flow: association cortex → entorhinal cortex → dentate gyrus → CA3 → CA1 → subiculum/entorhinal and fornical outputs, alongside important direct and recurrent pathways
clusters.project_relation: This gives the project's Memory rooms a genuine multi-stage return architecture rather than one hippocampus=memory equation.
clusters.boundary: Pattern separation/completion are useful computational descriptions, not exclusive functions of single subfields.

clusters.name: Cerebellar cortex, teaching signals and deep nuclei
clusters.summary: The cerebellum has a highly repeated microcircuit: mossy-fiber and climbing-fiber inputs shape granule/Purkinje processing, and Purkinje cells inhibit deep cerebellar nuclei that generate most cerebellar outputs.

core_elements.name: Mossy fibers
roles: broad sensory/cortical/contextual input via granule cells

core_elements.name: Granule cells / parallel fibers
roles: expanded distributed representation to Purkinje dendrites

core_elements.name: Climbing fibers
roles: powerful instructive/error-related input to Purkinje cells

core_elements.name: Deep nuclei
roles: major cerebellar outputs to thalamic/brainstem targets

clusters.project_relation: Correction/pruning/refinement gains a stronger biological neighbor here: prediction-error learning changes future output without implying moral correction.
clusters.boundary: The cerebellum is not merely a motor coordinator and its error signals are not theological judgment.

clusters.name: Pain, nociception and descending modulation
clusters.summary: Nociception is distributed across peripheral receptors, spinal/brainstem pathways, thalamus, cortex, limbic/interoceptive systems and descending modulatory circuits; pain is an experience, not a simple readout of tissue damage.
descending: rostral ventromedial medulla/raphe and noradrenergic brainstem systems
relations: attention, expectation, learning, threat and interoception shape pain
descending systems can facilitate as well as inhibit nociceptive transmission
clusters.project_relation: Pain belongs to the body's warning/report architecture, not a spiritual punishment axis.
clusters.boundary: Nociception and pain are related but not identical; theological or moral meanings must not be inferred from pain biology.

clusters.name: Neurovascular and metabolic coupling
clusters.summary: Neural activity depends on continuous energy delivery. Neurovascular coupling adjusts local cerebral blood flow through interactions among neurons, astrocytes, vascular cells and signaling molecules.
clusters.relation_to_imaging: BOLD fMRI is an indirect hemodynamic/metabolic signal related to neural activity, not a direct photograph of thoughts.
clusters.project_relation: Flow and Garden-support metaphors fit better here than claims of mystical brain energy: viable neural computation requires circulation, exchange and maintenance.
clusters.boundary: Blood flow is not consciousness, and fMRI activation is not a direct measure of spiritual intensity.

clusters.name: Development, maturation, plasticity and aging
clusters.summary: The brain changes throughout life through neurodevelopment, synaptogenesis, pruning, myelination, learning-related plasticity, hormonal transitions and aging-related structural/functional change.
clusters.project_relation: Seed → growth → pruning → mature Tree is a legitimate developmental metaphor only at the level of change over time.
clusters.boundary: Development does not encode a predetermined spiritual rank or destiny.

clusters.name: Language as a distributed network
clusters.summary: Language depends on distributed frontal, temporal, parietal, auditory, motor and white-matter systems rather than two isolated Broca/Wernicke boxes.
components: arcuate/superior longitudinal and ventral association pathways
clusters.project_relation: Word/witness symbolism can be compared with distributed language production and reception, but there is no single anatomical Word center.
clusters.boundary: Classic lesion models remain useful historically but are incomplete accounts of language organization.

clusters.name: Social cognition and theory-of-mind systems
clusters.summary: Understanding agents, intentions, emotion and social context recruits distributed medial prefrontal, temporoparietal, superior temporal, limbic, insular and default-network-related systems.
clusters.project_relation: Observer, witness and relation motifs can use social cognition as a scientific neighbor without equating mind-reading metaphors with literal neural telepathy.
clusters.boundary: There is no single theory-of-mind organ; tasks and network definitions vary.

clusters.name: Predictive processing / active inference — theory layer
clusters.status: theoretical framework, not settled anatomical fact
clusters.summary: Predictive-processing families model perception/action as hierarchical inference in which expectations interact with sensory evidence and prediction errors; active-inference formulations additionally model action as changing sampled states to reduce expected discrepancies under a generative model.
clusters.usefulness: This is a strong scientific-theory neighbor for the project's Observer/world-model language because it emphasizes recurrent top-down/bottom-up exchange rather than passive reception.
clusters.project_relation: Observer/world-model ↔ generative-model metaphor may be explored as a formal comparator.
clusters.boundary: Predictive processing is a family of models with active debate over scope, implementation and falsifiability; it must not be presented as proof of Potato Dynamics, God, or metaphysical manifestation.

cross_links: cranial nerves ↔ brainstem nuclei ↔ body interfaces
inferior olive ↔ climbing fibers ↔ Purkinje cells ↔ deep nuclei ↔ thalamus
entorhinal cortex ↔ dentate/CA3/CA1/subiculum ↔ distributed memory networks
neural activity ↔ astrocytes/neurovascular unit ↔ local blood flow
language/social networks ↔ large-scale cortical network architecture
